subject: Operational Compass: week of 2026-10-12 — wins, blockers & QBR asks
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Operational Compass: week of 2026-10-12 — wins, blockers & QBR asks

Team —

Quick signal for the week. TL;DR: solid progress on Dedicated onboarding, an infra capacity pinch that could surface after traffic spike, and two QBR asks for ACME that need content and a single POC. Please scan the bullets and call out anything that needs an exec decision.

Wins:
- Dedicated deployment for customer Atlas (internal pilot) is live in us-west-2; baseline latency down ~18% in our synthetic tests.
- CS completed the first pass of the ACME migration checklist; no major gaps identified.

Risks / blockers:
- Infra: we have one node-type (A100-80GB pool) with ~85% committed headroom on peak training window. If ACME expands concurrency in the QBR demo, we may breach our SLOs.
- QBR content: ACME asked to see cost/perf comparisons vs their incumbent; we need a consolidated slide and 1-page appendix by Wednesday.

Asks (owners + due dates):
- Karthik: please validate capacity forecasts and propose a short-term mitigation (burst pool or pre-warm nodes). Due: Tue COB 10/13. Attach okrs-weekly-heatmap.xlsx for numbers.
- Jonas: own a 1-page runbook for ACME demo fallbacks (what we switch to if we see latency > 250ms). Due: Wed 10/14 morning.
- Laura: confirm whether we can commit a one-time credit (up to $X) for the pilot if ACME requests it during QBR. Need direction by Wed EOD so we can finalize ask with procurement.

Attachments: QBR_prep_template_v3.pdf (slides), okrs-weekly-heatmap.xlsx (capacity numbers) — linked in the Drive below.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick sync Tue 8:30am PST (15m) to confirm capacity plan and the ask to ACME.
- Neha to draft the QBR slide and share with ACME for review by Thu.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational Compass: week of 2026-10-12 — wins, blockers & QBR asks

Thanks Neha — good summary. Two quick notes:

1) If ACME asks for a credit, we should prefer a pilot-performance tied credit rather than an upfront concession. I don't need the final numbers today, but please frame the ask that way.
2) For the capacity mitigation, if pre-warm is going to cost material $ and we can't get procurement sign-off fast enough, let's consider a temporary routing policy (route lower-priority demo traffic to a smaller model variant) as a fallback.

I'll be on the Tue 8:30 sync.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational Compass: week of 2026-10-12 — wins, blockers & QBR asks

Looking at the numbers in okrs-weekly-heatmap.xlsx — confirmed: peak concurrency from the pilot could push A100-80GB pool to ~98% if ACME runs two parallel demos. Options I have: 

A) Short-term: spin up a two-node burst pool (estimated incremental cost ~48 hours worth of reserved price) and auto-drain after the demo window.
B) Short-term alt: pre-warm a smaller model shard (quantized) and route demo traffic there — ~10–12% perf degradation but much lower cost and immediate.
C) Medium term: move ACME demo to dedicated reserved node group (requires contract amendment).

I recommend B for now (fastest and lowest friction). I'll draft the runbook for the switch and include metrics for rollback triggers. Attaching the capacity sheet excerpt.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Infra & Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Evan Holt <evan.holt@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Operational Compass: week of 2026-10-12 — wins, blockers & QBR asks

Hi Neha — thanks for the update. Two asks from our side prior to the QBR:
1) Can you include a simple cost vs performance slide comparing Redwood vs our current provider? We just need ballpark numbers for total cost of ownership over the pilot month.
2) Can we schedule the live demo for Thu 10/15 10am PT? That time works for our execs.

If you can share a deck and confirm the time, we'll lock the QBR slot.

Best,
Evan Holt
Director, Data & AI | ACME Corporation
